instructions.content: NEVER assume a technology stack without discovery; run discovery commands and map docs to the detected stack
NEVER dump encyclopedic content into root AGENTS.md; keep root concise and link to scoped files or references
NEVER duplicate the same instructions across root and sub-files; keep universal rules at root and package-specific rules locally
NEVER provide unverified commands; include only validated copy-paste commands
NEVER create a hierarchy for a simple, uniform project; use one root AGENTS.md when stack and patterns are uniform
NEVER put package-specific rules in the root file; keep package commands in that package's own AGENTS.md
NEVER use generic placeholder commands or paths; write the real path and command found during discovery
NEVER front-load every sub-file at once; start minimal and add scoped files iteratively as complexity grows
NEVER leave documentation stale after major repository changes; re-run discovery, remove obsolete content and document new scripts
Discover repository shape and technologies first, and decide between a simple and a hierarchical documentation strategy
Select the structure: a single root file for a simple project, or a root file plus scoped subdirectory files for a complex monorepo
Generate AGENTS.md content with concrete commands and paths, using JIT indexing to point at deeper detail
Validate command correctness and duplication boundaries so instruction files are copy-paste-safe
Re-check the documentation after major repo changes so it stays synchronised
Keep instructions concise, concrete, and path-specific
Prefer references and indices over duplicated prose
Optimise for nearest-file relevance in hierarchical layouts
Locate existing AGENTS.md or AI-DOCS.md files before creating new ones
Verify the finished files with markdownlint and the project's lint script
